statements.status_notes: GHSA-x4vx-rjvf-j5p4 affects DOMPurify IN_PLACE mode when sanitizing attacker-supplied live DOM nodes with clobbered nodeName properties. The Argo CD web UI uses DOMPurify to sanitize HTML strings rendered in the application interface, not IN_PLACE mode with attacker-controlled live DOM objects from same-origin subcontexts. No upstream npm release with a fix is available yet; this will be patched once dompurify ships a fixed version.

GHSA-x4vx-rjvf-j5p4 affects DOMPurify IN_PLACE mode when sanitizing attacker-supplied live DOM nodes with clobbered nodeName properties. The Argo CD web UI uses DOMPurify to sanitize HTML strings rendered in the application interface, not IN_PLACE mode with attacker-controlled live DOM objects from same-origin subcontexts. No upstream npm release with a fix is available yet; this will be patched once dompurify ships a fixed version.

No upstream fix is available: the dompurify advisory (GHSA-x4vx-rjvf-j5p4) lists no patched release and the latest version 3.4.9 remains affected. The XSS bypass via SVG use element requires attacker-controlled HTML content. In Uptime Kuma, dompurify sanitizes notification message content configured by authenticated administrators rather than anonymous attacker-controlled input. Reachability and a non-breaking mitigation are under assessment; this will be patched once dompurify ships a fix.
